name: ReconstructionSession
description:
Scenario 5: HoloMap Reconstruction
Purpose: Gold-standard fixture for the Sprint-3 decorator->trait
resolution pipeline. Proves the parser surface for
@reconstruction_source / @acceptance_video / @drift_corrected
decorators round-trips cleanly through the
parseHolo -> getReconstructionTraitsFromDecorators ->
generateHoloSource path.
Complexity: Single Node carrying the full decorator trio plus a
secondary Node carrying only @drift_corrected, exercising
both the multi-decorator union and the single-decorator
passthrough.
Sprint:     3 (Foundations Phase 3) — closes board task ghw9.
Related:
- packages/core/src/traits/constants/holomap-reconstruction.ts
- packages/core/src/traits/constants/__tests__/holomap-reconstruction.test.ts (Sprint 3 _xn9o)
- packages/core/src/reconstruction/RFC-HoloMap.md

ACCEPTANCE: when all 3 decorators are applied to a single Node, the
resolved HoloMap trait set MUST equal the full HOLOMAP_RECONSTRUCTION_TRAITS
list (5 traits, deduplicated, first-seen order). Round-tripping the file
through generateHoloSource MUST preserve the decorator set on each Node.

description:
Industrial Expansion POC — Refreshed
A009 Phase 2 — 2026-05-16

Original: digital-twin floor with Safety Warden LLM agent.
Refresh adds:
@emotion_directive — Warden face/body reflects alert level (neutral → concerned → alarmed)
@bloom_reactive    — machine emission scales live with vibration telemetry
@webcam_gaze       — operator console gaze-tracks engineer's eye direction,
highlights the machine they're looking at for digital record-keeping
@heatmap_3d        — machine shells display temperature hotspot overlays

Scene story: late-night shift on a chemical processing floor. Three machines
hum under sparse sodium-vapor lights. Pump-B vibration climbs past threshold.
The bloom on its housing flares amber. The Warden's expression shifts from
neutral to "concerned" as they cross the floor. The engineer at the control
console glances at Pump-B — the webcam gaze system highlights it for the log.

console glances at Pump-B — the webcam gaze system highlights it for the log.

name: ExhibitBase
description:
WCAG 2.1 Level AA Compliant Museum Scene
Exercises all 10 HoloScript accessibility traits in a realistic virtual museum

Accessibility traits demonstrated:
1. @accessible       - ARIA semantics, keyboard navigation, focus management
2. @alt_text         - Alternative text descriptions for 3D objects
3. @screen_reader    - Semantic structure for blind/low-vision navigation
4. @subtitle         - Real-time speech-to-text for deaf/hard-of-hearing
5. @high_contrast    - High contrast mode for low-vision visitors
6. @motion_reduced   - Reduced motion for vestibular sensitivity
7. @haptic_cue       - Non-visual haptic cues for interactions
8. @haptic           - Proximity and collision haptic feedback
9. @voice_input      - Voice command navigation
10. @voice_output     - Text-to-speech audio descriptions and narration

WCAG 2.1 AA criteria addressed:
1.1.1  Non-text Content          - @alt_text on every exhibit object
1.2.1  Audio-only / Video-only   - @voice_output audio descriptions
1.3.1  Info and Relationships     - @screen_reader semantic structure
1.3.2  Meaningful Sequence        - @accessible tab_index ordering
1.4.3  Contrast (Minimum)         - @high_contrast 4.5:1 ratio
1.4.4  Resize Text                - Font scaling via AccessibilitySystem
1.4.11 Non-text Contrast          - @high_contrast outline on UI
2.1.1  Keyboard                   - @accessible keyboard_shortcut
2.3.1  Three Flashes              - @motion_reduced disable parallax
2.4.1  Bypass Blocks              - @accessible skip-nav landmark
2.4.3  Focus Order                - @accessible tab_index sequence
2.4.6  Headings and Labels        - @accessible role + label
2.4.7  Focus Visible              - @accessible focus_visible
2.5.1  Pointer Gestures           - @voice_input alternative input
3.1.1  Language of Page           - i18n locale on composition
3.3.2  Labels or Instructions     - @accessible description
4.1.2  Name, Role, Value          - @accessible role, label, value
4.1.3  Status Messages            - @accessible live_region

description:
Asset Pipeline Warehouse

The HoloScript asset-production pipeline rendered as a walkable manufacturing
line. Each colour-coded station is one pipeline stage; an asset entity travels
the conveyor through them (driven at runtime via the world-state loop), so the
pipeline becomes a spatial, walkable thing in VR.

Native HoloScript — authored in .holo, loaded by the immersive viewer. No
inline scene strings. Stations laid out left -> right in front of the spawn
point (camera near z=4 looking toward -z); the asset flows along z=-4.

Stages: Generate -> Ingest -> Optimize -> Validate -> Provenance -> Publish.

outdoor_weather_zone
description:
============================================================================
Spatial Audio Showcase — Concert Hall (Premiere Night Refresh)
A-009 Phase 2 refresh — 2026-05-03

Original: concert hall spatial audio (7 traits).
Refresh intent: same hall, same audience seat — but it is the world
premiere of a new piano concerto on a January night. Sleet falls
outside. Guests arrive through the lobby, carrying storm acoustics
with them; the inner doors bleed muffled applause and instrument
warm-up through @audio_portal. A passing taxi triggers @doppler on
the street layer. The foyer zone uses @environmental_audio to model
cold humid air (high-frequency absorption), storm weather modulation,
and Doppler pitch shifts before the sound crosses into the dry,
reverberant concert hall.

New in this refresh:
@environmental_audio  — outdoor weather acoustics + air absorption
+ Doppler for the taxi passing outside
@room_mode_resonance  — sub-200Hz standing-wave / Helmholtz
resonance with modal frequency/Q data and
optional bass-node heatmap output

Traits covered (9 total):
@ambisonics         @hrtf           @reverb_zone
@audio_occlusion    @audio_portal   @audio_material
@head_tracked_audio @environmental_audio @room_mode_resonance
============================================================================

PortalAgent
description:
Agent Portal Federation — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates inter-scene agent communication via the AgentPortalTrait.
WHY .hsplus: Portal connections are inherently stateful (disconnected,
connecting, connected, migrating) with event-driven transitions that
require reactive state machines. Neither .holo (static scene) nor
.hs (sequential script) can express connection lifecycle guards,

name: CulturalAgent
description:
Cultural Evolution — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates emergent agent culture using CultureTraits (cultural_profile,
norm_compliant, cultural_memory, cultural_trace).
WHY .hsplus: Cultural evolution is a multi-agent reactive process where
agents observe norms, adapt behavior, and propose new norms over time.
Each agent progresses through a cultural evolution state machine
(newcomer -> observing -> adapting -> established -> norm_proposer)
with event-driven transitions triggered by norm compliance scores,
cultural memory consolidation, and stigmergic trace encounters.
.holo cannot express norm enforcement or adaptation; .hs cannot
express concurrent per-agent cultural state machines.

Features:
- NormEngine module for compliance evaluation and enforcement
- CulturalMemory module with episodic decay, consolidation, and traces
- Three agents with different cultural_family profiles
- Compatibility warnings between incompatible cultures
- Norm proposal and adoption lifecycle
- Spatial cultural_trace markers for stigmergic communication

@version 5.0.0
@format .hsplus (behavior)

name: SmartNPC
description:
Feedback-Driven NPC — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates a self-improving NPC that uses the FeedbackLoopTrait to
monitor performance metrics, detect trends, and auto-tune its own
parameters to maintain quality targets.
WHY .hsplus: Self-optimization is an inherently reactive, stateful
process. The NPC's performance level (degraded -> baseline -> optimized
-> peak) transitions are driven by continuous metric collection,
trend analysis, and threshold-triggered optimization signals -- all
event-driven patterns that require state machines and @on_update
loops. .holo is static; .hs is one-shot. Only .hsplus can express
the continuous feedback cycle.

Features:
- MetricsCollector module for FPS, engagement, latency, memory tracking
- TrendAnalyzer module with linear regression and trend detection
- AutoTuner module for generating and applying optimization signals
- NPC state machine: degraded -> baseline -> optimized -> peak
- @on_update for continuous metric collection
- @on_event for user feedback (ratings, interactions)
- Reactive HUD panels showing real-time performance

name: SecureAgent
description:
Secure Agent Handshake — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates post-quantum cryptographic authentication using ML-DSA-65,
Ed25519 hybrid signing, ML-KEM-768 key exchange, and token-based
session management.
WHY .hsplus: Cryptographic handshakes are textbook state machines.
The authentication lifecycle (idle -> key_exchange -> challenge ->
verified -> session_active -> rotating -> expired) has strict ordering
(cannot verify before key exchange), timeout guards (challenge must
complete within window), and periodic key rotation timers that require
@on_update. Token expiry is event-driven. Neither .holo (no state)
nor .hs (no timers or concurrent sessions) can express this.

Features:
- KeyManager module for ML-DSA-65 + Ed25519 hybrid key generation
- SessionManager module for token creation, validation, and expiry
- SecureAgent template with authentication state machine
- @on_event handlers for auth lifecycle events
- Token types: agent_auth, session, capability
- Key rotation timer with @on_update
- Two agents demonstrating mutual authentication

@version 5.0.0
@format .hsplus (behavior)

LifecycleController
description:
Enterprise Tenant Lifecycle — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates multi-tenant management with the TenantTrait and RBAC
system for enterprise deployments.
WHY .hsplus: Tenant provisioning, suspension, and deletion are
multi-step workflows with strict ordering constraints (cannot archive
without suspending first, cannot delete without archiving). Role
transitions require approval guards (viewer -> editor needs admin
approval). These lifecycle constraints are naturally expressed as
state machine guards. The audit trail requires event-driven logging
of every state change. Neither .holo nor .hs can express guarded
multi-actor state machines with audit event streams.

Features:
- TenantManager module for tenant CRUD and lifecycle
- RBACEngine module for role assignment, permission checks, transitions
- AuditLogger module for comprehensive event logging
- Tenant lifecycle state machine with ordering guards
- RBAC role transition sub-state-machine with approval workflow
- @tenant with enterprise configuration

description:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
UNITY HDRP EXPORT PIPELINE - Enterprise Asset Integration
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Demonstrates complete Unity HDRP project export with:
- C# MonoBehaviour components
- HDRP material conversion (PBR → Lit shader)
- Prefab generation with nested hierarchies
- Animation controller setup
- Physics components (Rigidbody, Collider)
- Audio source configuration
- Lighting and post-processing volumes
- TextMeshPro UI integration

Compilation:
holoscript compile --target unity --hdrp export-to-unity.holo

Output:
- UnityHDRPScene.prefab (main scene prefab)
- Assets/Materials/*.mat (HDRP Lit materials)
- Assets/Scripts/*.cs (generated C# components)
- Assets/Animations/*.anim (animation clips)

    geometry: "cube"
    position: [3, 0, 1]
    scale: [1, 1, 2]

    material_unreal: {
      parent_material: "M_MasterMaterial_Translucent"
      material_domain: "surface"
      blend_mode: "translucent"
      shading_model: "default_lit"

      translucent_shadow_density_scale: 0.5
      translucent_self_shadow_density_scale: 2.0
      translucent_self_shadow_second_density_scale: 10.0

      // Material properties
      base_color: [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
      metallic: 0.0
      roughness: 0.1
      opacity: 0.3

      // Refraction
      refraction_mode: "index_of_refraction"
      index_of_refraction: 1.5

      // Lumen translucency
      lumen_translucency_reflections: true
      lumen_translucency_frontlayer: true
    }
  }

UNREAL ENGINE 5 EXPORT PIPELINE - AAA Game Production Asset Integration
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Demonstrates complete Unreal Engine 5 project export with:
- C++ Actor classes with BlueprintCallable functions
- Blueprint Actor components (visual scripting support)
- Nanite-enabled high-poly meshes
- Lumen global illumination setup
- Enhanced Input System integration
- Niagara particle systems
- Chaos physics with destruction
- MetaSounds audio system
- Control Rig skeletal animation
- Data Assets and DataTables

Compilation:
holoscript compile --target unreal --ue5 export-to-unreal.holo

Output:
- Content/Blueprints/BP_UnrealScene.uasset (Blueprint Actor)
- Source/HoloScript/*.h, *.cpp (C++ Actor classes)
- Content/Materials/M_*.uasset (Material instances)
- Content/Meshes/SM_*.uasset (Static meshes with Nanite)
- Content/Niagara/NS_*.uasset (Particle systems)
- Content/Animations/*.uasset (Animation sequences)
- Content/Audio/MS_*.uasset (MetaSounds)

Unreal Requirements:
- Unreal Engine 5.0+ (UE5.1+ for Nanite/Lumen full features)
- Enhanced Input Plugin enabled
- Niagara Plugin enabled (default)
- Chaos Destruction Plugin (optional, for destructible meshes)

name: CharacterRoot
description:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
FBX ANIMATION EXPORT - 3D DCC Tool Interchange Pipeline
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Demonstrates complete FBX export for:
- Maya, 3ds Max, Blender, Cinema 4D
- MotionBuilder (animation editing)
- Unity, Unreal, Godot (game engines)
- Houdini (procedural workflows)
- ZBrush (high-poly sculpting round-trip)
- Substance Painter (texture baking)

FBX Features Demonstrated:
- Skeletal animation (joints, skinning, IK)
- Blend shapes (morph targets, facial animation)
- Animation layers and takes
- Keyframe interpolation (linear, bezier, TCB)
- Constraints (parent, aim, orient, scale)
- Inverse Kinematics (IK chains)
- Animation baking (FK to baked FK, IK to FK)
- Material preservation (Phong, Lambert, PBR)
- Embedded media (textures in .fbx)
- Multiple UV sets
- Vertex colors
- Normals and tangents

Compilation:
holoscript compile --target fbx fbx-animation-export.holo
holoscript compile --target fbx --ascii fbx-animation-export.holo  # ASCII FBX

Output:
- character.fbx (Binary FBX 2020)
- character_ascii.fbx (ASCII FBX for debugging)
- textures/*.png (Embedded or referenced)
- character.xml (FBX SDK metadata)

Compatible Software:
- Autodesk Maya 2018+
- Autodesk 3ds Max 2018+
- Blender 2.8+
- Cinema 4D R20+
- Houdini 18+
- MotionBuilder 2018+
- Unity 2019+
- Unreal Engine 4.25+
- Godot 3.2+

name: HealthPotion
description:
Dungeon Crawler State Machine — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates WHY .hsplus exists: reactive state machines with event-driven
transitions that neither .holo (too declarative) nor .hs (too sequential)
can express cleanly.

This is a complete dungeon crawler game with:
- Game state machine (menu → exploring → combat → inventory → victory → game_over)
- Wave spawner with timer-based enemy waves
- Inventory system with @stackable items and capacity limits
- Combat system with turn-based state transitions
- Score tracking with @observable state changes
- Multiplayer-ready with @networked state sync

name: ModernSofa
description:
AR Furniture Preview — Staged Three-Vignette Showroom
E-commerce AR experience for furniture visualization. The catalog is
arranged as a walkable showroom of three non-overlapping room vignettes,
each with one focal piece its accessories orient around:
LIVING (x≈0)  — sofa facing a coffee table on a rug, floor lamp beside it, pendant overhead
DINING (x≈+6) — dining table centered under its own pendant, chairs tucked in
BEDROOM (x≈-6) — bed flanked by nightstands, dresser against the wall, rug beneath
Previously the pieces were dumped into one overlapping space (a QueenBed at the
origin sat on top of the living-room sofa/rug) so it read as a pile, not a showroom.
This pass also fixes duplicate object names: the two "FloorLamp" objects are now
LivingFloorLamp / DiningFloorLamp, and the two "DiningChair2" objects are now
EamesChairB (living/dining accent) / WindsorChair2 (dining set). Every object name is unique.
Only names, positions, rotations, and scales changed — all materials, behaviors, and systems are intact.
Platform targets: ARKit, ARCore, WebXR

E-commerce AR experience for furniture visualization. The catalog is
arranged as a walkable showroom of three non-overlapping room vignettes,
each with one focal piece its accessories orient around:
LIVING (x≈0)  — sofa facing a coffee table on a rug, floor lamp beside it, pendant overhead
DINING (x≈+6) — dining table centered under its own pendant, chairs tucked in
BEDROOM (x≈-6) — bed flanked by nightstands, dresser against the wall, rug beneath
Previously the pieces were dumped into one overlapping space (a QueenBed at the
origin sat on top of the living-room sofa/rug) so it read as a pile, not a showroom.
This pass also fixes duplicate object names: the two "FloorLamp" objects are now
LivingFloorLamp / DiningFloorLamp, and the two "DiningChair2" objects are now
EamesChairB (living/dining accent) / WindsorChair2 (dining set). Every object name is unique.
Only names, positions, rotations, and scales changed — all materials, behaviors, and systems are intact.
Platform targets: ARKit, ARCore, WebXR

  }

AR Furniture Preview — Staged Three-Vignette Showroom
E-commerce AR experience for furniture visualization. The catalog is
arranged as a walkable showroom of three non-overlapping room vignettes,
each with one focal piece its accessories orient around:
LIVING (x≈0)  — sofa facing a coffee table on a rug, floor lamp beside it, pendant overhead
DINING (x≈+6) — dining table centered under its own pendant, chairs tucked in
BEDROOM (x≈-6) — bed flanked by nightstands, dresser against the wall, rug beneath
Previously the pieces were dumped into one overlapping space (a QueenBed at the
origin sat on top of the living-room sofa/rug) so it read as a pile, not a showroom.
This pass also fixes duplicate object names: the two "FloorLamp" objects are now
LivingFloorLamp / DiningFloorLamp, and the two "DiningChair2" objects are now
EamesChairB (living/dining accent) / WindsorChair2 (dining set). Every object name is unique.
Only names, positions, rotations, and scales changed — all materials, behaviors, and systems are intact.
Platform targets: ARKit, ARCore, WebXR

name: GalleryFloor
description:
Contemporary Masters — a processional route, not a floor plan.
The visitor enters south under the EntranceArch, is drawn down the
entry axis (z) to the HERO piece — Sculpture2, the $45k "Ascending
Form" bronze — set on-axis and lit hardest. The PartitionWall is the
SPINE that bends the path left around itself, past a sequence of
subordinate sculptures, and out through the gift shop at the NE
corner. Seating and lighting are handed toward the hero: nothing is
mirror-symmetric. One decision governs — a directed path culminating
in a single centerpiece.
Platforms: Unity, Unreal, BabylonJS, WebXR

name: GoldTerrace
description:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE GOLD GAME — Gate 16: the Vault soundscape (REAL Godot audio path).

The audio layer for the vault, authored on the REAL HoloScript audio
substrate (physics-upward: model the acoustics, don't just attach clips).
This .holo is the source the REAL GodotCompiler turns into Godot audio nodes:
- top-level `audio "Name" { spatial: true ... }`  → AudioStreamPlayer3D
- top-level `audio "Name" { ... }`                 → AudioStreamPlayer (2D)
- `@audio_material` / `@audio_occlusion` / `@audio_portal` on surfaces
→ acoustic traits emitted into the GDScript (config preserved).

Sources + acoustics are exactly the AUDIO-vault.md design:
ambient bed (2D), per-tier music (2D), graduation cue (spatial 3D — THE
signature SFX), crystal-spire shimmer (3D), collision clang (3D),
Archivist presence (3D). Gold terraces = metal acoustics; gems = glass;
tier portals route sound zone-to-zone as you ascend.

HONEST: Godot is the one shipped audio compiler target — these nodes are
real. The web/R3F Drive build is silent (no audio compiler path); a small
WebAudio layer is the build target. No TTS/voiced lines; no adaptive
@MusicLayer — tier music is static per-tier sources, flagged not faked.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE GOLD GAME — Gate 0 canonical skeleton (FOUNDER-RATIFIED CONCEPT 2026-05-22)

The flagship is the REAL GOLD knowledge-curation system (D:/GOLD) turned into
a GAME the founder plays, while the SAME system is enhanced for the agents/AI
who use it. Professional-system-as-game (the HoloLand/HoloShell pattern):
the human plays; the AI runs the real vault underneath.

REAL BACKEND  ⇄  GAME FACE (human)        ⇄  AGENT ENHANCEMENT
tiers bronze→diamond  →  ascending regions you climb   →  visible progression
graduate.py           →  THE CORE VERB: shepherd an     →  cleaner graduation
entry up the tiers                workflow
auto_link / lineage   →  forge the constellation of     →  richer retrieval
links between entries             graph
vault_collision_guard →  conflicts to resolve (monsters)→  de-duped vault
agents curating       →  real-agent co-players          →  game-shaped curation

HONEST MAPPING IS THE PRODUCT: a play-action IS a real vault op (graduating an
entry in-game graduates it for real). Reads the REAL vault as content; never
fakes vault state. Writing back to D:/GOLD stays governance-gated.

Seeded with real vault entries (INDEX.md): P.GOLD.001 (Diamond), W.GOLD.535,
W.GOLD.534, B.GRADUATE.001 (Bronze). Tier reality per `farm.py status`.

DEPLOYMENT (founder-ratified): compiles to a self-contained static web build
(R3F → index.html) destined for the D: Drive so it opens on any machine with
no install. Engine target = r3f; packaging target = portable Drive build.

AI<->HUMAN CONNECTION (load-bearing): one CURATOR entity kind, two inhabitation
paths (human @controllable / agent @ai_agent) acting on the SAME real vault.

Gate 0 acceptance = parses clean against @holoscript/core. Branding is a

name: Research_Floor
description:
=============================================================================
VR Agent Motivation Visualizer
=============================================================================
Real-time display of active reward signals per agent in a multi-agent
HoloLand world. Each agent has a floating sphere showing motivation state:
- Position: X = intrinsic motivation, Y = social motivation, Z = task motivation
- Color: blended gradient reflecting reward signal strength (dim=low, bright=high)
- Ring size: confidence / belief update magnitude
- Animated "flow" particles: reward gradient descent trajectory
- Heartbeat beacon: agent presence + communication link

Use case: AI researchers visualizing emergent multi-agent motivation in
collaborative VR environments. Real-time binding to agent observation streams.
=============================================================================

name: photo_plane
description:
Depth Estimation Hologram Demo

The trait computes a real-time depth map using Depth Anything V2 Small.
The resulting depth map drives parallax displacement for a hologram-like
3D-from-2D effect, with reactive colour and opacity bindings.

name: Dashboard_Floor
description:
=============================================================================
HoloScript VR Training Pipeline Dashboard
=============================================================================
Spatial visualization of the HoloLand self-improve + harvest pipeline.

Renders a VR dashboard showing:
- 6 VR domain category stations (spatial-rendering, avatar-systems, etc.)
- Real-time harvest pipeline progress (captured/accepted/rejected)
- Frame budget compliance gauges per domain (11.1ms @ 90Hz)
- Quality score convergence trajectory (3D line chart)
- Training data output stream visualization
- Domain coverage heatmap

Designed for Quest 3 at 90Hz with foveated rendering.
Budget: 11.1ms total frame, 5.5ms splat rendering (per G.003.09).
=============================================================================

V&V Results Visualization Space
=============================================================================

walk through convergence plots in 3D, compare mesh refinement levels
visually, and see uncertainty distributions as volumetric clouds around
simulation results.

Three major zones:
1. Convergence Gallery   - 3D convergence plots as walkable landscapes
2. Mesh Refinement Arena - Side-by-side mesh levels with exploded views
3. Uncertainty Cloud Lab - Volumetric probability clouds around results

Data binding: connects to SimSci solver outputs via @data_binding traits.

Immersive VR environment for Verification & Validation professionals to
walk through convergence plots in 3D, compare mesh refinement levels
visually, and see uncertainty distributions as volumetric clouds around
simulation results.

Three major zones:
1. Convergence Gallery   - 3D convergence plots as walkable landscapes
2. Mesh Refinement Arena - Side-by-side mesh levels with exploded views
3. Uncertainty Cloud Lab - Volumetric probability clouds around results

Designed for Quest 3 at 90Hz. Frame budget: 11.1ms.
Data binding: connects to SimSci solver outputs via @data_binding traits.
=============================================================================

description:
HoloTwin Example: Smart Farm Sensor Dashboard

Demonstrates IoT sensor → HoloScript scene → Looking Glass quilt pipeline.
Three sensors (temperature, humidity, soil moisture) drive 3D visualization.

Usage:
1. Load in Studio: holoscript studio --load examples/iot/holotwin-smart-farm.holo
2. Connect to MQTT broker: mqtt://farm.local:1883
3. Sensors auto-publish to topics: farm/sensor/{temperature,humidity,moisture}
4. Quilt compiles automatically and displays on Looking Glass

Or use MCP tools:
holo_holotwin_connect(physicalId="farm-001", protocol="mqtt", connectionString="mqtt://farm.local:1883")
holo_holotwin_map_sensor(sessionId, mappings=[...])
holo_holotwin_compile_quilt(sessionId, holoCode)

name: Camera
Root: Parser
description:
============================================================================
The Lotus Flower — Living Visualization of the 16-Paper Research Program
============================================================================
Brittney's garden. Each petal is a paper; each petal's bloom-state is
derived from real evidence (commit hashes, anchor receipts, benchmark
presence, audit-matrix rows).

Brittney CANNOT lie about a petal's bloom — the state is a pure function
of repo evidence (see `packages/studio/src/lib/brittney/lotus/derive-bloom-state.ts`).
She tends the garden by reading evidence and proposing what's needed for
the next bloom; she cannot bloom a petal that the evidence doesn't justify.

Why a lotus: per `docs/strategy/lotus-architecture.md`, the program is one
architecture (provenance semiring) demonstrated through 16 papers. Roots =
substrate, stalk = formats (.hs/.hsplus/.holo/.hs.md), petals = papers,
center = Dumb Glass (rendering as contracted synthesis).

description:
The Lotus Flower — SEEDABLE STAGED ARTIFACT (Pre-Genesis)

staged: true
Composed by /artist on 2026-05-06 per idea-run-11 form recommendation
(research/2026-05-06_idea-run-11-lotus-seedable-artifact.md).

RELATIONSHIP TO BASELINE:
This file is NEW and DOES NOT replace garden.refreshed.holo.
`garden.refreshed.holo` (A-009 baseline, 2026-05-04) remains the
bloom-state visual-readability reference and is NOT touched here.
`garden.seedable.holo` adds the seedable mathematical-sculpture
spine + Fibonacci-layered petals + deterministic placement on top
of A-009's glow/pulse/pollen vocabulary.

FORM (per /idea memo):
Hybrid: golden-angle phyllotaxis spine + Fibonacci-layered petals
(8 inner + 13 middle + 21 outer = 42 petals = 3 program-tiers ×
Fibonacci sequence) + GPUParticleTrait pollen field + @bloom_reactive
driving petal opacity from program-progress signal.

Petal placement is a PURE FUNCTION of LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED. Same seed →
same composition byte-for-byte. Pre-genesis: seed = 0x0000DEAD
(placeholder per project_lotus-genesis-trigger.md). Post-genesis:
seed = first-16-bytes(events.jsonl[0].hash). Staged-vs-live transition
is zero-code-change at composition level — the renderer swaps the seed.

DETERMINISM CONTRACT:
- Petal positions: golden-angle 137.50776° spiral, indexed globally
across layers (continuous spiral, not per-layer reset).
- Layer radii: [2.0, 3.4, 4.8] (Fibonacci-derived: 2, 3+1, 5-0.2).
- Layer counts: [8, 13, 21] (Fibonacci sequence F6/F7/F8, mapping
to Programs 1/2/3 by capacity-not-current-content).
- Bloom-state per petal driven by `lotus.api.bloom_state` signal
(already wired in packages/studio/src/lib/brittney/lotus/derive-bloom-state.ts).
- Jitter / particle seed / pollen drift PRNG: SeedHKDF(LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED,
petal_index). Staged seed produces deterministic but visibly muted
palette so genesis-fired version reads as a phase change.

I.007 CONSTRAINTS PRESERVED:
- SDF center body deferred to Phase 2 (placeholder mesh until genesis fires).
- GenesisLightColumn declared but `enabled: false` until trigger.
- Genesis chime audio at volume 0.0 until `all_petals_full`.
- Outer-layer (21 petals, Program 3) starts FULLY SEALED — these are
the future capacity slots, named but not paper-bound.

FRAME-DRIFT NOTE (W.137):
Trait-binding TODOs below are migration markers, not proof that the
substrate is absent. @botanical_lotus / @lotus_root / @lotus_stalk /
@lotus_petal / @lotus_center / @lotus_gardener / @phyllotaxis /
@bloom_reactive / @lotus_genesis_trigger now have backed runtime handlers.
@lotus_genesis_trigger is still founder-gated and cannot fire without a
signed genesis anchor plus all-petals-full state.
This artifact remains STAGED because the live trait blocks, genesis seed,
and final photoreal material pipeline are still gated.

RELATIONSHIP TO BASELINE:
This file is NEW and DOES NOT replace garden.refreshed.holo.
`garden.refreshed.holo` (A-009 baseline, 2026-05-04) remains the
bloom-state visual-readability reference and is NOT touched here.
`garden.seedable.holo` adds the seedable mathematical-sculpture
spine + Fibonacci-layered petals + deterministic placement on top
of A-009's glow/pulse/pollen vocabulary.

FORM (per /idea memo):
Hybrid: golden-angle phyllotaxis spine + Fibonacci-layered petals
(8 inner + 13 middle + 21 outer = 42 petals = 3 program-tiers ×
Fibonacci sequence) + GPUParticleTrait pollen field + @bloom_reactive
driving petal opacity from program-progress signal.

Petal placement is a PURE FUNCTION of LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED. Same seed →
same composition byte-for-byte. Pre-genesis: seed = 0x0000DEAD
(placeholder per project_lotus-genesis-trigger.md). Post-genesis:
seed = first-16-bytes(events.jsonl[0].hash). Staged-vs-live transition
is zero-code-change at composition level — the renderer swaps the seed.

DETERMINISM CONTRACT:
- Petal positions: golden-angle 137.50776° spiral, indexed globally
across layers (continuous spiral, not per-layer reset).
- Layer radii: [2.0, 3.4, 4.8] (Fibonacci-derived: 2, 3+1, 5-0.2).
- Layer counts: [8, 13, 21] (Fibonacci sequence F6/F7/F8, mapping
to Programs 1/2/3 by capacity-not-current-content).
- Bloom-state per petal driven by `lotus.api.bloom_state` signal
(already wired in packages/studio/src/lib/brittney/lotus/derive-bloom-state.ts).
- Jitter / particle seed / pollen drift PRNG: SeedHKDF(LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED,
petal_index). Staged seed produces deterministic but visibly muted
palette so genesis-fired version reads as a phase change.

I.007 CONSTRAINTS PRESERVED:
- SDF center body deferred to Phase 2 (placeholder mesh until genesis fires).
- GenesisLightColumn declared but `enabled: false` until trigger.
- Genesis chime audio at volume 0.0 until `all_petals_full`.
- Outer-layer (21 petals, Program 3) starts FULLY SEALED — these are
the future capacity slots, named but not paper-bound.

`garden.refreshed.holo` (A-009 baseline, 2026-05-04) remains the
bloom-state visual-readability reference and is NOT touched here.
`garden.seedable.holo` adds the seedable mathematical-sculpture
spine + Fibonacci-layered petals + deterministic placement on top
of A-009's glow/pulse/pollen vocabulary.

FORM (per /idea memo):
Hybrid: golden-angle phyllotaxis spine + Fibonacci-layered petals
(8 inner + 13 middle + 21 outer = 42 petals = 3 program-tiers ×
Fibonacci sequence) + GPUParticleTrait pollen field + @bloom_reactive
driving petal opacity from program-progress signal.

Petal placement is a PURE FUNCTION of LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED. Same seed →
same composition byte-for-byte. Pre-genesis: seed = 0x0000DEAD
(placeholder per project_lotus-genesis-trigger.md). Post-genesis:
seed = first-16-bytes(events.jsonl[0].hash). Staged-vs-live transition
is zero-code-change at composition level — the renderer swaps the seed.

DETERMINISM CONTRACT:
- Petal positions: golden-angle 137.50776° spiral, indexed globally
across layers (continuous spiral, not per-layer reset).
- Layer radii: [2.0, 3.4, 4.8] (Fibonacci-derived: 2, 3+1, 5-0.2).
- Layer counts: [8, 13, 21] (Fibonacci sequence F6/F7/F8, mapping
to Programs 1/2/3 by capacity-not-current-content).
- Bloom-state per petal driven by `lotus.api.bloom_state` signal
(already wired in packages/studio/src/lib/brittney/lotus/derive-bloom-state.ts).
- Jitter / particle seed / pollen drift PRNG: SeedHKDF(LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED,
petal_index). Staged seed produces deterministic but visibly muted
palette so genesis-fired version reads as a phase change.

I.007 CONSTRAINTS PRESERVED:
- SDF center body deferred to Phase 2 (placeholder mesh until genesis fires).
- GenesisLightColumn declared but `enabled: false` until trigger.
- Genesis chime audio at volume 0.0 until `all_petals_full`.
- Outer-layer (21 petals, Program 3) starts FULLY SEALED — these are
the future capacity slots, named but not paper-bound.

FRAME-DRIFT NOTE (W.137):
Trait-binding TODOs below are migration markers, not proof that the
substrate is absent. @botanical_lotus / @lotus_root / @lotus_stalk /
@lotus_petal / @lotus_center / @lotus_gardener / @phyllotaxis /
@bloom_reactive / @lotus_genesis_trigger now have backed runtime handlers.
@lotus_genesis_trigger is still founder-gated and cannot fire without a
signed genesis anchor plus all-petals-full state.
This artifact remains STAGED because the live trait blocks, genesis seed,
and final photoreal material pipeline are still gated.

FORM (per /idea memo):
Hybrid: golden-angle phyllotaxis spine + Fibonacci-layered petals
(8 inner + 13 middle + 21 outer = 42 petals = 3 program-tiers ×

(placeholder per project_lotus-genesis-trigger.md). Post-genesis:
seed = first-16-bytes(events.jsonl[0].hash). Staged-vs-live transition
is zero-code-change at composition level — the renderer swaps the seed.

- Petal positions: golden-angle 137.50776° spiral, indexed globally
across layers (continuous spiral, not per-layer reset).
- Layer radii: [2.0, 3.4, 4.8] (Fibonacci-derived: 2, 3+1, 5-0.2).
- Layer counts: [8, 13, 21] (Fibonacci sequence F6/F7/F8, mapping
to Programs 1/2/3 by capacity-not-current-content).
- Bloom-state per petal driven by `lotus.api.bloom_state` signal
(already wired in packages/studio/src/lib/brittney/lotus/derive-bloom-state.ts).
- Jitter / particle seed / pollen drift PRNG: SeedHKDF(LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED,
petal_index). Staged seed produces deterministic but visibly muted
palette so genesis-fired version reads as a phase change.

the future capacity slots, named but not paper-bound.

(research/2026-05-06_idea-run-11-lotus-seedable-artifact.md).

RELATIONSHIP TO BASELINE:
This file is NEW and DOES NOT replace garden.refreshed.holo.
`garden.refreshed.holo` (A-009 baseline, 2026-05-04) remains the
bloom-state visual-readability reference and is NOT touched here.
`garden.seedable.holo` adds the seedable mathematical-sculpture
spine + Fibonacci-layered petals + deterministic placement on top
of A-009's glow/pulse/pollen vocabulary.

FORM (per /idea memo):
Hybrid: golden-angle phyllotaxis spine + Fibonacci-layered petals
(8 inner + 13 middle + 21 outer = 42 petals = 3 program-tiers ×
Fibonacci sequence) + GPUParticleTrait pollen field + @bloom_reactive
driving petal opacity from program-progress signal.

Petal placement is a PURE FUNCTION of LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED. Same seed →
same composition byte-for-byte. Pre-genesis: seed = 0x0000DEAD
(placeholder per project_lotus-genesis-trigger.md). Post-genesis:
seed = first-16-bytes(events.jsonl[0].hash). Staged-vs-live transition
is zero-code-change at composition level — the renderer swaps the seed.

DETERMINISM CONTRACT:
- Petal positions: golden-angle 137.50776° spiral, indexed globally
across layers (continuous spiral, not per-layer reset).
- Layer radii: [2.0, 3.4, 4.8] (Fibonacci-derived: 2, 3+1, 5-0.2).
- Layer counts: [8, 13, 21] (Fibonacci sequence F6/F7/F8, mapping
to Programs 1/2/3 by capacity-not-current-content).
- Bloom-state per petal driven by `lotus.api.bloom_state` signal
(already wired in packages/studio/src/lib/brittney/lotus/derive-bloom-state.ts).
- Jitter / particle seed / pollen drift PRNG: SeedHKDF(LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED,
petal_index). Staged seed produces deterministic but visibly muted
palette so genesis-fired version reads as a phase change.

I.007 CONSTRAINTS PRESERVED:
- SDF center body deferred to Phase 2 (placeholder mesh until genesis fires).
- GenesisLightColumn declared but `enabled: false` until trigger.
- Genesis chime audio at volume 0.0 until `all_petals_full`.
- Outer-layer (21 petals, Program 3) starts FULLY SEALED — these are
the future capacity slots, named but not paper-bound.

name: GameLobby
description:
Multiplayer Arena Game — Refreshed (A-009 refresh 2026-05-25)

Original intent: a networked 2-player arena where each player grabs a ball
and tries to throw it through the opponent's goal.

Refresh adds:
@lobby          — pre-game lobby with skill-based matchmaking and a 10-second
countdown before play begins. Exercises zero-coverage trait.
@networked_avatar — each spawn point hosts a synchronized avatar with full
skeletal IK — hands follow tracked controllers. Zero-coverage.
@haptic         — GameBall triggers controller rumble on grab and on goal impact.
@state_machine  — Arena transitions: Lobby → Countdown → Playing → Scored → End.
@particle       — goal rings emit a burst of team-colored sparks on score.

Scene story: a compact hexagonal arena suspended in void. Two players materialize
at their glowing spawn discs — blue and orange. Before the timer hits zero, avatars
can wave their hands; IK bones follow tracked controllers in real time. Kick-off:
the ball drops center. On impact with the net the goal ring detonates in sparks and
the arena state machine advances to Scored, pausing physics for two seconds before
the next serve. Controller haptics confirm every catch and every score.

name: MysticalGlowFlicker
description:
Narrative Events — The Shattered Crown
Refreshed by A-009 on 2026-05-04

Refresh delta: Replaced generic narrator scaffolding with a concrete
three-act mystery scene. Added @reactive to interactive story objects so
flashback triggers fire when the player *approaches* them (not just on
manual trigger). Added @state_machine to drive act transitions cleanly.
Added @spatial_audio depth to the moonlit court. Added @emissive to
foreshadowing artifacts so visual hints are legible without subtitles.

Scene story: The player discovers the throne room of a ruined castle.
Three shattered relics each hold a memory fragment — approaching each
triggers a flashback. Collect all three to unlock the fourth act: the
truth of the crown's fall. The night sky shifts color as acts progress.

@version 5.2.0
@format .holo
@traits @reactive, @state_machine, @spatial_audio, @emissive, @animated,
@glowing, @particle, @clickable

name: NetworkConfig
description:
============================================================================
Multiplayer Authority Demo
============================================================================
Demonstrates HoloScript's networking authority traits for multiplayer
scenes. Shows owner authority, server authority, shared editing, and
ownership transfer patterns for networked objects.

Traits covered (2 missing traits + authority patterns):
@owned        -- Object has a specific owner (client authority)
@host_only    -- Object only exists / is visible on the host
@networked    -- Base networking with configurable authority modes

Authority modes demonstrated:
owner    -- Only the owning client can modify
server   -- Host is authoritative; clients send requests
shared   -- Any client can modify with CRDT conflict resolution
============================================================================

name: GovernanceHall
description:
Cultural Governance Demo

Demonstrates HoloScript's Norm Lifecycle DSL extension for declarative
cultural engineering using the CRSEC model:
C - Creation:       How norms are proposed and authored
R - Representation: Formal encoding of rules and constraints
S - Spreading:      How norms propagate through agents
E - Evaluation:     Voting rules and adoption thresholds
C - Compliance:     Enforcement, violations, and sanctions

Also demonstrates metanorms (norms about norms) for governance
of the norm system itself.

Use Cases:
- Multi-agent virtual communities with self-governance
- AI agent societies with emergent social norms
- Collaborative VR workspaces with behavioral standards
- Gaming worlds with player-driven rule systems

name: CalmMeadow
description:
Neurodiverse Adaptive Therapy Worlds

TherapyCompanion agents with cultural + sensory adjustment traits adapt
particle density, haptics, color spectrum, and audio in real time for
neurodiverse users. They migrate across home Quest → clinic visionOS →
school WebXR with full session state. EconomyPrimitives let users "pay"
agents in credits for session continuity; FeedbackLoop auto-tunes based
on biometric/user-rating loops. TenantTrait enables HIPAA compliance.

"Build a therapy world where AI companions adapt colors, sounds,
and particles for neurodiverse users. Let the companion migrate
between my home headset, clinic, and school. Track biometric
calm scores and auto-adjust."

- AWE Auggie "Best Healthcare & Wellness"

name: GuideAgent_VR
description:
============================================================================
Cross-Reality Agent Continuity — Full-Stack Demo
============================================================================
Demonstrates an AI guide agent that persists seamlessly across:
VR headset → AR glasses → Phone → Desktop → Car → Wearable

Features exercised:
- @platform() conditional compilation with category-level filtering
- MVC handoff payload (<10KB) with decision history + task state
- Embodiment transitions (Avatar3D → SpatialPersona → UI2D → VoiceHUD)
- CRDT-backed spatial anchors for shared world state
- Norm lifecycle (CRSEC) for agent behavior governance
- Offline recovery queue for airplane mode resilience

name: TableBase
description:
============================================================================
Retro Pinball Table — Synthwave Edition
A-009 refresh — 2026-06-01

Original intent: complete pinball game with physics, game state, and
interactive bumpers, targets, flippers, and scoring.

Refresh adds:
@morph         — pop bumpers squish/pop on ball contact (blend shapes)
@sonification  — ball velocity magnitude mapped to synthesizer pitch
@bloom_reactive — score digits and bumpers pulse on point events

Scene story:
The same retro pinball table, but now it plays itself like a living
instrument. As the ball gathers speed across the table, the sonification
engine bends a sawtooth wave from a low 60 Hz drone to a piercing 880 Hz
scream. Each bumper hit squishes the geometry down and rebounds it
upward in a satisfying micro-animation. The scoreboard digits pulse like
a heart — each point scored lights them briefly to 3x normal intensity
before fading back. The table is no longer just a game; it is a
score-driven musical machine.

name: Floor
description:
Brittney Playground — embodied-agent testing room.

A native HoloScript scene where Brittney (the flagship agent, D.094) is embodied
as a tracked AgentAvatar and moves under her own native .hsplus brain
(examples/agents/brittney-playground.hsplus, driven via the world-state loop). The
Waypoint_* pads are her patrol path — read from THIS scene (single source of truth)
by scripts/brittney-brain-driver.mjs, so moving a pad moves her route.

Walkable: the shared @holoscript/xr-embodiment locomotion lets you walk the room
(left stick) and watch her presence move. The body is a placeholder orb today; the
AAA avatar (brittney-avatar.holo) swaps into the same AgentAvatar slot later.
snippet:
object "Floor" {
    geometry: "plane"
    position: [0, 0, -4]
    scale: [16, 1, 16]
    color: "#15151f"
    material: "StudioConcrete"
  }

name: BaseLink

Target platform: NVIDIA Isaac Sim (PhysX physics)
Compile with: holoscript compile --target urdf --isaac-sim isaac-sim-robot-arm.holo

Features demonstrated:
- Unique material names (prevents Isaac Sim material merging)
- Proper inertia tensors (not simplified mass * 0.1)
- PhysX-optimized collision geometry
- ROS 2 control integration
- Fixed frames for end effector and sensor mounts

name: Painting
description:
============================================================
"Neon Horizon" — a single-artist retrospective
============================================================
BRIEF (the referent, not the label): not "a gallery" but ONE
curated show. The centerpiece work, "Neon Horizon," hangs on
the north wall and the whole room is staged to serve it.
The one decision everything else obeys: an ENTRY SIGHTLINE.
The visitor enters from the south and looks straight down
the axis (-z) into a HERO WALL — one large centerpiece
flanked by two SMALLER studies. Not five equal canvases;
a show with a reading order: hero first, side studies next,
the two subordinate west/east works last.
Governed by that decision: the sculpture is pushed OFF the
central axis so it never blocks the hero sightline; the
lighting is weighted onto the centerpiece instead of spread
evenly; a single bench sits on the axis FACING the hero so a
viewer can sit and contemplate it. The room has a clear
FRONT (hero wall) and BACK (entrance), not four equal sides.
Every @advanced_pbr material and all @clickable/@hoverable
behavior is unchanged — this pass reshapes the STAGING to the
brief, not the surfaces.
============================================================

name: OfficeChair
description:
============================================================
Multiplayer Meeting Room - HoloScript Sample Project
============================================================
A professional virtual conference room designed for multi-
user collaboration. Features a conference table with chairs,
a shared whiteboard, avatar spawn points, spatial audio
zones, and networked objects that stay synchronized across
all connected clients.

PRESENTATION-FOCUS ORIENTATION: the room has a front. The
whiteboard (north wall, z=-4) and presentation screen (east
wall, x=+5) form a north-east presenter corner, and the room
addresses it. A head-of-table seat anchors the far (west/south)
end, remaining seats fan toward that corner facing the
presenter, the table skews to point at it, and ceiling lighting
is weighted over the presentation end and the table rather than
spread as an even grid.
============================================================

A professional virtual conference room designed for multi-
user collaboration. Features a conference table with chairs,
a shared whiteboard, avatar spawn points, spatial audio
zones, and networked objects that stay synchronized across
all connected clients.

PRESENTATION-FOCUS ORIENTATION: the room has a front. The
whiteboard (north wall, z=-4) and presentation screen (east
wall, x=+5) form a north-east presenter corner, and the room
addresses it. A head-of-table seat anchors the far (west/south)
end, remaining seats fan toward that corner facing the
presenter, the table skews to point at it, and ceiling lighting
is weighted over the presentation end and the table rather than
spread as an even grid.
============================================================

object "WallSouth" @collidable {
    geometry: "cube"
    position: [0, 1.6, 4]
    scale: [10, 3.2, 0.12]
    color: "#bdc3c7"
    material: "OfficeDrywall"
  }

name: GiVolume
description:
============================================================================
Solar System — Physically-Based Orrery
A-009 refresh — 2026-05-17

Original intent: Keplerian orbital mechanics for inner planets + Moon.
Refresh adds:
@atmosphere_bruneton — Mie+Rayleigh sky on Earth (blue limb) and Mars (rust limb)
@day_night_cycle     — Earth rotates; city-lights texture on night side
@irradiance_volume   — Sun-driven planetary bounce light captured in GI probes
@emissive_gi         — Sun's self-illumination contributes outward to GI probes
@lens_flare          — solar lens flare when camera faces the Sun

Scene story:
You drift in space between Venus and Earth. The Sun blazes ahead, its corona
blooming with lens flare arcs. Earth hangs blue and white — day side shining,
night side jewelled with city lights, its Rayleigh-blue limb distinguishing it
instantly from the rust-limbed Mars further out. The Moon traces its tilted
5° orbit. An instanced asteroid belt scatters debris between 1.9–2.8 AU.

Bruneton atmosphere gives Earth a proper scattering limb and Mars a thin
reddish haze. The irradiance volume captures Solar bounce light so the dark
side of each planet picks up a faint warm ambient. The day/night cycle on
Earth switches to city-lights texture as each hemisphere turns away from the Sun.

@corona_simulation now shipped (A-009, 2026-06-09):
Procedural solar corona with MHD flux-tube loops, streamer belt,
coronal hole polar plumes, and CME event trigger API.
See packages/core/src/traits/CoronaSimulationTrait.ts
============================================================================

A-009 refresh — 2026-05-17

Original intent: Keplerian orbital mechanics for inner planets + Moon.
Refresh adds:
@atmosphere_bruneton — Mie+Rayleigh sky on Earth (blue limb) and Mars (rust limb)
@day_night_cycle     — Earth rotates; city-lights texture on night side
@irradiance_volume   — Sun-driven planetary bounce light captured in GI probes
@emissive_gi         — Sun's self-illumination contributes outward to GI probes
@lens_flare          — solar lens flare when camera faces the Sun

Scene story:
You drift in space between Venus and Earth. The Sun blazes ahead, its corona
blooming with lens flare arcs. Earth hangs blue and white — day side shining,
night side jewelled with city lights, its Rayleigh-blue limb distinguishing it
instantly from the rust-limbed Mars further out. The Moon traces its tilted
5° orbit. An instanced asteroid belt scatters debris between 1.9–2.8 AU.

Bruneton atmosphere gives Earth a proper scattering limb and Mars a thin
reddish haze. The irradiance volume captures Solar bounce light so the dark
side of each planet picks up a faint warm ambient. The day/night cycle on
Earth switches to city-lights texture as each hemisphere turns away from the Sun.

@corona_simulation now shipped (A-009, 2026-06-09):
Procedural solar corona with MHD flux-tube loops, streamer belt,
coronal hole polar plumes, and CME event trigger API.
See packages/core/src/traits/CoronaSimulationTrait.ts
============================================================================
snippet:
object "Moon" {
    geometry: "sphere"
    material: { baseColor: "#AAAAAA", roughness: 0.9, metallic: 0.05 }
    scale: 0.27

    parent: "Earth"
    semiMajorAxis: 0.002570
    eccentricity: 0.054900
    inclination: 5.145
    longitudeAscending: 125.08
    argumentPeriapsis: 318.15
    meanAnomalyEpoch: 135.27
    orbitalPeriod: 27.321
    rotationPeriod: 27.321

    @orbital()
  }

name: LighthouseBeacon
description:
============================================================================
A-009 Stress Test — 2026-05-04
"Abyssal Expedition"

NEW TRAITS EXERCISED (zero prior coverage across ALL examples today):
@submarine      — maritime: pressurized vessel with depth/sonar systems
@buoy           — maritime: surface marker beacon with tether physics
@lighthouse     — maritime: rotating navigation beam, fog signal
@kraken         — mythical: ancient cephalopod intelligence, tentacle rig
@wraith         — mythical: non-corporeal shadow entity, phase shift
@phoenix        — mythical: fire-and-rebirth creature, cyclic lifecycle

Supporting traits (well-exercised, binding the new ones into a scene):
@glowing, @particle, @spatial_audio, @physics, @animated, @collidable,
@emissive, @reactive

SCENE STORY:
The research submersible NAUTILIS-7 descends the Hadal Trench,
breaching three thermocline layers into the aphotic zone. On the
surface, a fleet of navigational buoys marks the dive corridor;
an autonomous lighthouse beacon on the seamount lip guides the
ascent path back.

Below 6 000 m, bioluminescent colonies carpet the walls. Then
the sonar goes wide: the Kraken — not a myth but a cephalopod
macro-intelligence — surfaces from the sediment. Its eight arms
(each a separate tentacle physics rig) surround the submarine.
The lights die. In the dark, a Wraith coalesces — spectrographic
residue of a crew lost decades ago, phase-shifting through the
hull. And at the thermal vent on the trench floor, a Phoenix
rises: plasma-hot gas vents cycling in a 90-second death-and-rebirth
loop, carving an updraft that sends the submarine spiraling upward.

ARTISTIC INTENT:
Three mythological archetypes mapped to real deep-ocean phenomena:
Kraken  → colonial intelligence, distributed cognition
Wraith  → electromagnetic residue, sensor ghosts
Phoenix → hydrothermal cycling, life from superheated vents
The submersible is the human witness — fragile, pressurized, lit
from inside. The maritime navigation layer (lighthouse, buoys)
frames the scale: surface is safety, depth is wonder-and-terror.

COMPILE TARGET: @target webgpu (volumetric water, GPU particle budget)
============================================================================

name: MilkyWayDome
description:
============================================================================
Stress-Test: Alpine Observatory at Midnight
A-009 Phase 3 — 2026-05-19

Trait combo (NEVER previously exercised together):
@aurora            (0 prior examples) — soft northern-lights curtain on
the northern horizon, green-to-magenta band, 3-4 Hz
shimmer, does not wash the zenith stars.

@starfield         (0 prior examples) — procedural star catalogue, 8,200
stars above magnitude 6.5. Milky Way band rendered as
a volumetric noise lane with dust extinction.

@meteor_shower     (0 prior examples) — Perseid radiant at Perseus (RA 3h
04m, Dec +58°), 80 km altitude ablation trails,
2–4 sec burn with magnesium-white to orange-red fade.

@ambisonics        (0 prior examples) — 2nd-order (FOA+) ambisonics
captures observatory dome acoustics: concrete floor
reverb, metal dome ring, wind directionality.
Binaural decode on headset, stereo decode otherwise.

@chromatic_aberration (0 prior examples) — subtle prismatic fringing at
the eyepiece view edge; triggers momentarily on dome
rotation events, simulating refractive lens shift.

@iridescent        (0 prior examples) — thin-film oil-and-dew sheen on
the cold aluminium dome skin; shifts between green,
gold, and violet as the viewing angle changes.

Well-exercised anchors (pull the zero-coverage traits into proven context):
@glowing     (726 prior) — instrument panel warm amber glow; eyepiece
red-light safety lamp
@animated    (271 prior) — dome drive motor rotation; wind-flag ripple
@collidable  (664 prior) — observatory floor, dome walls, telescope mount
@spatial_audio (77 prior)— point-source wind whistle at dome slit edge

Visual story:
02:47 local. You stand on the concrete floor of a stone observatory at
3,100 m in the Swiss Alps. The slit is open — a 30° wedge of sky
visible directly overhead. The Milky Way stretches through it in
startling density: not a smear but individual star lanes, the dark rift
of the dust cloud bisecting the band from Sagittarius to Cygnus.

A Perseid burns through your slit at 02:47:13. Two seconds of
magnesium-white ablation, decaying through yellow to orange-red, then
gone. The trail lingers as a ghost smear for five seconds more. You
blink. The dark-adapted eye takes thirty seconds to recover magnitude 6.

On the northern horizon — just visible through the slit's edge — a pale
green aurora ribbon hangs at 110 km altitude. It is not dramatic. It is
precisely the dim, wavering kind that real aurora-watchers wait all night
for, faint enough that you question whether it is there, then certain
when the 3 Hz shimmer catches your eye.

The dome skin is cold — 4°C. Dew has condensed on it since 23:00. You
hear the dome drive motor click: the RA axis is tracking, advancing the
dome slot 4 arcminutes every 16 seconds to keep the slit aligned with
the telescope. As the dome moves, the iridescent dew film shifts color
— green to gold to violet — visible through the observation window.

You remove your eye from the eyepiece. The sudden shift from the dark-
adapted ocular field to the ambient dome red-lights sends a brief wave
of chromatic aberration: the nearby instrument panel's amber light
splits into red-fringing on the left, blue on the right, for ~1.4 sec.

Ambisonics: the dome is acoustically interesting. Wind from the west
whistles at the slit's northern lip — you hear it above-left. The
concrete floor gives a flat reflection below. The metal dome curves
sound around you. Take off headphones: it still sounds right. Put them
on: it is spatial, enveloping, cold.
============================================================================
snippet:
object "MilkyWayDome" {
    type: "sky_sphere"
    radius: 5000

    @starfield(
      catalogue: "hipparcos_subset",
      magnitude_limit: 6.5,
      star_count: 8200,
      scintillation: true,
      scintillation_speed: 0.8,
      scintillation_amplitude: 0.12,
      milky_way: {
        enabled: true,
        band_intensity: 0.55,
        dust_extinction: true,
        dust_density: 0.38,
        core_glow_color: "#ffd8a8",
        arm_color: "#c8d8ff"
      },
      atmosphere_extinction: true,
      horizon_fade_degrees: 12
    )
  }

name: surgical_key
description:
============================================================
Stress-Test: Holographic Anatomy Theater
A-009 — 2026-05-03

Never-exercised traits under test:
@subsurface_veins    — procedural vascular tree renderer,
heartbeat-pulsed subsurface absorption
@volumetric_window   — visionOS spatial window management:
bounded / volumetric / world-scale
@diffusion_realtime  — LCM / StreamDiffusion real-time AI
texture streaming at interactive fps

Well-exercised anchors:
@glowing  @grabbable  @collidable

Visual story:
A surgical education suite for Apple Vision Pro — clean clinical
white, warm theatre lighting. Three floating windows hover above
a teaching table at the centre of the room. Each window is a
@volumetric_window spatial container at a different scale mode.

Window A (world-scale): a stylised human heart in cross-section.
@subsurface_veins renders 50 K vascular segments, the coronary
arteries lit from inside, pulsing at 72 BPM. The resident can
grab the heart, rotate it, and watch the blood-lit veins shift
under the skin surface with each heartbeat.

Window B (tabletop-scale): a sagittal brain slice.
@subsurface_veins at 28 K segments traces the dural venous
sinuses and cortical microvasculature, slower pulse (65 BPM),
with a cooler blue vein tint for venous blood.

Window C (room-scale): a live histology feed.
A 512 × 512 @diffusion_realtime stream runs a txt2img LCM
pipeline, generating photorealistic H&E staining slides at
~15 fps. The prompt is steered by the instructor. This window
is @glowing — the AI slide emits a faint warm light into the
room as it generates.

All three anatomy objects are @grabbable: attendees can rearrange
the layout during the session.

This is the first time @subsurface_veins, @volumetric_window,
and @diffusion_realtime are exercised in any example.

Parse targets:
(a) @subsurface_veins: segmentCount int + pulseBpm float +
nested color { r g b } object — all single-line inline
(b) @volumetric_window: all-required enum fields on one line
(c) @diffusion_realtime: backend enum + string prompt fields

Parser note: all trait configs are placed inside object blocks
as inner directives (not inline decorators on the definition
line) with comma-separated single-line properties, which is
the pattern the current parser handles correctly. Multi-line
nested property objects require comma separation to parse.
============================================================
snippet:
object "surgical_key" {
    type: "point_light"
    color: "#f8f9fa"
    intensity: 5.0
    position: [0, 3.2, 0]
    castShadow: true
  }

name: CeilingRing
description:
The Cartographer's Table (A-009 stress-test 2026-05-25)

Exercises two zero-coverage trait combinations:
@world_generator    — generates 3D island geometry from text prompts via the
sovereign-3d engine; outputs Gaussian splat + mesh pair.
@screen_space_effects — full SSR + SSAO + film grain + depth-of-field stack
applied to the obsidian chamber.

Combined with well-exercised traits:
@glowing            — cartographic interface panels and island frames
@animated           — table surface pulses as generation runs
@particle           — data-dust scatters as each island crystallizes
@physics            — generated island chunks obey gravity, can shatter
@bloom_reactive     — bloom spikes at generation completion event

Scene story: a circular obsidian chamber, forty meters across. In the center
stands a low hexagonal table — the Cartographer's Table — ringed by six hovering
input panels. An operator presses a rune on panel three and speaks a biome:
"volcanic archipelago, low tide, active vents." The table surface blooms white.
Data-dust rises in a slow vortex — particles of shredded 3D Gaussian data,
recycled from the last generation run. Then the first island emerges: a basalt
stack four meters tall, steaming at the waterline, surrounded by smaller islets.
Each island floats at eye level. The operator can reach in and shatter one against
the table edge — physics fragments scatter, then the table absorbs them back into
the next prompt.

The chamber floor is polished black obsidian. SSR reflects the floating islands
perfectly. SSAO deepens the cracks between basalt columns. Depth of field pulls
the distant chamber wall soft, focusing the eye on the islands. Film grain recalls
the linen texture of early cartography.
snippet:
object "CeilingRing" {
    type: "ring_light"
    position: [0, 18, 0]
    inner_radius: 12.0
    outer_radius: 14.0
    color: "#6040c8"
    intensity: 0.6
  }

name: NexusRoom
description:
============================================================================
CONSENT NEXUS — The Ethics Commons
A-009 stress-test 2026-06-02

Traits exercised (all previously uncovered):
@blackboard     — shared spatial memory for collective agent intelligence
@crdt_room      — CRDT-backed multiplayer synchronisation
@consent_gate   — ethical consent lifecycle for sensitive AR/MR feeds

+ well-exercised grounding traits:
@networked @physics @spatial_audio @glowing @animated

Scene story:
You step into the Consent Nexus, a shared XR commons where collaboration
is made visible. A glowing blackboard floats at the center of the room —
agents post beliefs ("pathway clear", "resource pool at 84%") and
proposals ("migrate shard 3 to Pod B?") in real time. Every participant
can read and vote.  The entire room state is CRDT-synchronized: no
server bottleneck, no single point of failure — just convergent replicas
held together by vector clocks.

On entry, the room presents a Consent Manifesto: a set of capability
requests (camera feed for presence detection, microphone for voice-channel,
location for spatial anchoring). Each capability has a visual indicator
above the consent panel — green ring = granted, amber = pending, red =
denied.  No feed activates until a participant explicitly taps "Accept."

This scene exists to stress-test whether these three traits can coexist
on a single composition without compiler conflicts.
============================================================================

name: ServiceStrip_Port
description:
The Drift-Sleep Sanctuary (A-009 stress-test 2026-06-03)

NEVER-EXERCISED TRAITS UNDER TEST:

@cryo          — Two hundred and forty stasis pods line the curved walls
of Deck 7. Each pod is a sealed cryo-vessel: a titanium-
ceramic shell, double-walled with liquid helium coolant
cycling through micro-channels. The @cryo trait drives
the thermal state machine — target_temp_k, coolant_flow,
frost_accumulation, warming_rate, and the visual frost
bloom that spreads across the viewport glass when a pod
first seals. Three pods in the starboard aft bay are
showing amber status: their frost lines are too regular,
suggesting a micro-crack in the coolant jacket.
Exercises: target_temp_k, coolant_flow_lpm, frost_coverage,
frost_pattern, warning_threshold_k, warming_rate_k_per_min,
viewport_frost_material, leak_probability.

@stasis        — Each occupied pod holds a colonist in full biological
suspension: metabolism at 2 % of basal, core temperature
92 K, EEG flatline except for the low-frequency sleep
maintenance wave at 0.08 Hz that the system keeps
deliberately active — there is emerging evidence that
complete neural silence over multi-year transit causes
micro-structural hippocampal damage. The @stasis trait
manages the occupant's physiological state and the UI
readout visible through each frosted viewport.
Exercises: metabolic_rate_fraction, neural_maintenance_hz,
core_temp_k, elapsed_years, projected_wake_year,
vitals_display_mode, wake_protocol, emergency_wake_trigger.

@nanite        — The atmosphere of Deck 7 is not clean air. The ship's
maintenance nanites — model MN-440 "Shepherd" — swarm at
a density of roughly 10^8 per cubic metre: invisible
individually, collectively catching the blue service
lighting as a faint haze, a living smoke that thickens
near any surface that needs attention. The three amber
pods have a visible cloud of nanites orbiting them —
the swarm has detected the thermal anomalies and is
attempting micro-welding on the coolant jacket seams.
Exercises: density_per_m3, model_id, task_mode,
swarm_cohesion, visual_density_scale, task_target,
task_glow_color, task_radius, collision_avoidance.

@melancholic   — Scene-wide emotional register. A generation ship at
year 14 of a 60-year transit. No crew awake. The only
motion is the musicbot, the nanite haze, and the slow
pulse of pod status lights. @melancholic doesn't add
a filter — it adjusts the ambient hue balance toward
cool desaturated blue-grey, slightly reduces particle
brightness, and lowers post-processing bloom so that
the scene reads as quiet resignation rather than drama.
Exercises: intensity, hue_shift_deg, saturation_scale,
particle_brightness_scale, bloom_scale, affects_skybox.

@musical       — MusicBot-7 is the ship's sole active passenger. It
has no designated function during transit; it was
brought aboard by a colonist who then chose emergency
early stasis after the launch-window fever broke
badly. The bot patrols the cryo-deck on a 40-minute
loop, stopping at each occupied pod for approximately
11 seconds and playing 8 bars of a lullaby it composed
during the first week of transit. It has composed
1,847 variations since. The @musical trait drives its
output: instrument model, key, tempo, phrasing style,
and the volume envelope it uses to avoid harmonising
against the cryo-deck's own 40 Hz resonance.
Exercises: instrument, key, tempo_bpm, style,
volume_envelope, avoid_freq_hz, auto_compose,
compose_variation_seed, phrase_length_bars.

@rhythm        — The stasis-maintenance pulse for each pod fires at
0.08 Hz — one neural maintenance cycle every 12.5
seconds. The @rhythm trait wires MusicBot-7's phrase
cadence to that pulse: the last note of each 8-bar
phrase lands within 200 ms of the pod's maintenance
fire, so that the colonist's sleep-maintenance wave
and the musical phrase end together. All 240 pods are
slightly phase-offset from each other, so the deck
breathes in a slow, unsynchronised murmur. The bot
selects which pod to play to next by finding the one
whose next maintenance cycle is soonest.
Exercises: source_frequency_hz, target_tag, sync_mode,
phase_tolerance_ms, phase_lock_strength, cascade_radius,
rhythm_display_mode.

WELL-EXERCISED ANCHOR TRAITS:
@animated      — pod status light pulsing, nanite haze drift, frost spread
@glowing       — pod viewport edge glow (colour-coded: green=nominal,
amber=warn, blue=deep-cold), service lighting strips
@collidable    — pod shells, floor deck plates, musicbot chassis
@physics       — nanite swarm particle physics, musicbot locomotion
@spatial_audio — lullaby point-source from musicbot, cryo hum ambient,
nanite micro-welding hiss near amber pods

SCENE STORY:
Year 14. The *Perseverance* is 4.2 light-years from departure. The
cryo-deck smells of nothing — the air recycler keeps the atmosphere
sterile and at 7 °C, which is warm compared to the pods but cold
enough that each slow exhalation from the vents fogs briefly before
it mixes.

MusicBot-7 moves at 0.3 m/s, which is as fast as it has learned to
go without the pod-proximity sensors flagging it as a threat. It
stopped near Pod 114 three minutes ago. The occupant — Maya Osei,
37 at departure, architect — has her next maintenance pulse in 9
seconds. The bot's left manipulator is producing a G minor arpeggio
in its 1,847th variation on the original lullaby. The nanite haze
drifts through the blue service lighting in slow rivers, thickening
in the starboard aft corner where the amber pods are. No human is
awake to see any of it. No human will be awake for 46 more years.

COMPILE TARGET: webgpu / unity
@cryo requires a thermal material shader (frost bloom on viewport glass).
@nanite requires GPU-instanced particle simulation with task-routing logic.
@musical requires audio synthesis or sample playback with dynamic variation.
@rhythm requires a clock-sync subsystem wired to both audio and stasis state.

The Drift-Sleep Sanctuary (A-009 stress-test 2026-06-03)

NEVER-EXERCISED TRAITS UNDER TEST:

@cryo          — Two hundred and forty stasis pods line the curved walls
of Deck 7. Each pod is a sealed cryo-vessel: a titanium-
ceramic shell, double-walled with liquid helium coolant
cycling through micro-channels. The @cryo trait drives
the thermal state machine — target_temp_k, coolant_flow,
frost_accumulation, warming_rate, and the visual frost
bloom that spreads across the viewport glass when a pod
first seals. Three pods in the starboard aft bay are
showing amber status: their frost lines are too regular,
suggesting a micro-crack in the coolant jacket.
Exercises: target_temp_k, coolant_flow_lpm, frost_coverage,
frost_pattern, warning_threshold_k, warming_rate_k_per_min,
viewport_frost_material, leak_probability.

@stasis        — Each occupied pod holds a colonist in full biological
suspension: metabolism at 2 % of basal, core temperature
92 K, EEG flatline except for the low-frequency sleep
maintenance wave at 0.08 Hz that the system keeps
deliberately active — there is emerging evidence that
complete neural silence over multi-year transit causes
micro-structural hippocampal damage. The @stasis trait
manages the occupant's physiological state and the UI
readout visible through each frosted viewport.
Exercises: metabolic_rate_fraction, neural_maintenance_hz,
core_temp_k, elapsed_years, projected_wake_year,
vitals_display_mode, wake_protocol, emergency_wake_trigger.

@nanite        — The atmosphere of Deck 7 is not clean air. The ship's
maintenance nanites — model MN-440 "Shepherd" — swarm at
a density of roughly 10^8 per cubic metre: invisible
individually, collectively catching the blue service
lighting as a faint haze, a living smoke that thickens
near any surface that needs attention. The three amber
pods have a visible cloud of nanites orbiting them —
the swarm has detected the thermal anomalies and is
attempting micro-welding on the coolant jacket seams.
Exercises: density_per_m3, model_id, task_mode,
swarm_cohesion, visual_density_scale, task_target,
task_glow_color, task_radius, collision_avoidance.

@melancholic   — Scene-wide emotional register. A generation ship at
year 14 of a 60-year transit. No crew awake. The only
motion is the musicbot, the nanite haze, and the slow
pulse of pod status lights. @melancholic doesn't add
a filter — it adjusts the ambient hue balance toward
cool desaturated blue-grey, slightly reduces particle
brightness, and lowers post-processing bloom so that
the scene reads as quiet resignation rather than drama.
Exercises: intensity, hue_shift_deg, saturation_scale,
particle_brightness_scale, bloom_scale, affects_skybox.

@musical       — MusicBot-7 is the ship's sole active passenger. It
has no designated function during transit; it was
brought aboard by a colonist who then chose emergency
early stasis after the launch-window fever broke
badly. The bot patrols the cryo-deck on a 40-minute
loop, stopping at each occupied pod for approximately
11 seconds and playing 8 bars of a lullaby it composed
during the first week of transit. It has composed
1,847 variations since. The @musical trait drives its
output: instrument model, key, tempo, phrasing style,
and the volume envelope it uses to avoid harmonising
against the cryo-deck's own 40 Hz resonance.
Exercises: instrument, key, tempo_bpm, style,
volume_envelope, avoid_freq_hz, auto_compose,
compose_variation_seed, phrase_length_bars.

@rhythm        — The stasis-maintenance pulse for each pod fires at
0.08 Hz — one neural maintenance cycle every 12.5
seconds. The @rhythm trait wires MusicBot-7's phrase
cadence to that pulse: the last note of each 8-bar
phrase lands within 200 ms of the pod's maintenance
fire, so that the colonist's sleep-maintenance wave
and the musical phrase end together. All 240 pods are
slightly phase-offset from each other, so the deck
breathes in a slow, unsynchronised murmur. The bot
selects which pod to play to next by finding the one
whose next maintenance cycle is soonest.
Exercises: source_frequency_hz, target_tag, sync_mode,
phase_tolerance_ms, phase_lock_strength, cascade_radius,
rhythm_display_mode.

WELL-EXERCISED ANCHOR TRAITS:
@animated      — pod status light pulsing, nanite haze drift, frost spread
@glowing       — pod viewport edge glow (colour-coded: green=nominal,
amber=warn, blue=deep-cold), service lighting strips
@collidable    — pod shells, floor deck plates, musicbot chassis
@physics       — nanite swarm particle physics, musicbot locomotion
@spatial_audio — lullaby point-source from musicbot, cryo hum ambient,
nanite micro-welding hiss near amber pods

SCENE STORY:
Year 14. The *Perseverance* is 4.2 light-years from departure. The
cryo-deck smells of nothing — the air recycler keeps the atmosphere
sterile and at 7 °C, which is warm compared to the pods but cold
enough that each slow exhalation from the vents fogs briefly before
it mixes.

MusicBot-7 moves at 0.3 m/s, which is as fast as it has learned to
go without the pod-proximity sensors flagging it as a threat. It
stopped near Pod 114 three minutes ago. The occupant — Maya Osei,
37 at departure, architect — has her next maintenance pulse in 9
seconds. The bot's left manipulator is producing a G minor arpeggio
in its 1,847th variation on the original lullaby. The nanite haze
drifts through the blue service lighting in slow rivers, thickening
in the starboard aft corner where the amber pods are. No human is
awake to see any of it. No human will be awake for 46 more years.

COMPILE TARGET: webgpu / unity
@cryo requires a thermal material shader (frost bloom on viewport glass).
@nanite requires GPU-instanced particle simulation with task-routing logic.
@musical requires audio synthesis or sample playback with dynamic variation.
@rhythm requires a clock-sync subsystem wired to both audio and stasis state.
